subject: Too many conditional panels = slow app

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Too many conditional panels = slow app
parts:
This has come up before:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/slow/shiny-discuss/aKeHTI5pgWU/biyyIla1Uu0J

I often encounter similar issues with larger apps, but it does seem to be specifically due to conditional panels. I think this is what the browser profiling in telling me. Example Firefox in-browser profiling screenshot attached.

Can anyone confirm if this is correct and, if so, is there a better approach to using many conditional panels? I thought doing everything server-side by having all my conditional statements inside my reactive expressions would ultimately be slower. Perhaps there is a point where conditional panels become the bottleneck? Suggestions for best practices? A big app can have a few dozen conditional panels. Even if there is not much data or processing to do; it just seems to be too much conditional logic. Sometimes I will even nest them up to a total of three layers. Is this bad practice? It gives me exactly what I need in certain circumstances, but really slows down the launch of the app, during which time the user cannot interact with the browser in general.

Thanks,
Matt

Matt

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Re: Too many conditional panels = slow app
parts:
The response time is virtually instantaneous now.

For context, this is for a huge app with over 40 conditional panels, some nested up to three layers (and much server side conditional reactivity too), eight menus in the navbar, one with nine submenus to individual markdown documents, and with use of navbarPage() nested inside of fluidPage() so that I can still have full control over sidebars and main panels and such based on tabPanel id from the navbar. Also using the new shinythemes package.

Awesome. You guys shaved off all 40 of the 40 seconds lag!

Thanks,
Matt

On Wednesday, February 4, 2015 at 11:27:12 AM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
We've merged a fix for this issue into master, and would appreciate it if you tried it out. You can install with:
  devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')

The new fix should be as fast or faster than the previous fix that you tried out.

Thanks!
-Winston

On Tue, Feb 3, 2015 at 12:59 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
We have a couple more fixes coming today that should knock down most of the remaining three seconds, hopefully. Thanks for bearing with us.

On Tue, Feb 3, 2015 at 10:58 AM, Matthew Leonawicz <mfleo...@alaska.edu> wrote:
Wow! This is much better! It's gone from a 35-40 second freeze that occurred a couple seconds after launch to now down to a total of about five seconds. I use system.time() in the log to track time for things like sourcing .RData files or anything potentially concerning that may eat up time before an app is fully running. For this app that is two of those five seconds. So essentially only three seconds for whatever was previously taking 35-40.

Thanks for your help and your quick replies,
Matt


On Tuesday, February 3, 2015 at 10:25:16 AM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
Matthew, I think this is related to some other reported issues, and we have a possible fix. Could you give it a try, with the instructions here?
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/717#issuecomment-72679878

On Mon, Feb 2, 2015 at 8:42 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

I see what the problem is. I'll take a stab at solving this tomorrow. Thanks so much for the screenshots, that was hugely helpful.

On Feb 2, 2015 6:02 PM, "Matthew Leonawicz" <mfleo...@alaska.edu> wrote:
Regarding the profiling sampling, the slow portion takes about 35 seconds instead of 45 when not profiling. Shorter, but still long. I can time it without profiling because it kicks in about two seconds after the app first opens in a browser tab and finishes when the browser becomes responsive again.

Matt

On Monday, February 2, 2015 at 6:55:25 PM UTC-7, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
Sorry, I failed to see that one was not expanded. New screenshot attached. The tree expands quite a ways. I am unsure if it is indicative of the complexity of my app and/or if this means the problem is unrelated to my initial suspicion about the conditional panels.

Matt

On Monday, February 2, 2015 at 6:26:24 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

Can you send another screenshot, this time with the updateConditional subtree expanded until you see something with a significant self time or large number of samples?

This of time is really unexpected and out of control, we should just fix it.

On Feb 2, 2015 5:06 PM, "Matthew Leonawicz" <mfleo...@alaska.edu> wrote:
This has come up before:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/slow/shiny-discuss/aKeHTI5pgWU/biyyIla1Uu0J

I often encounter similar issues with larger apps, but it does seem to be specifically due to conditional panels. I think this is what the browser profiling in telling me. Example Firefox in-browser profiling screenshot attached.

Can anyone confirm if this is correct and, if so, is there a better approach to using many conditional panels? I thought doing everything server-side by having all my conditional statements inside my reactive expressions would ultimately be slower. Perhaps there is a point where conditional panels become the bottleneck? Suggestions for best practices? A big app can have a few dozen conditional panels. Even if there is not much data or processing to do; it just seems to be too much conditional logic. Sometimes I will even nest them up to a total of three layers. Is this bad practice? It gives me exactly what I need in certain circumstances, but really slows down the launch of the app, during which time the user cannot interact with the browser in general.

Thanks,
Matt
